newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr regains footing, solid job ads help.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr regains footing, solid job ads help.

text.p: The Australian dollar shrugged off early selling to reclaim the US$0.7830 level at the midsession aided by a startlingly strong partial data on the labour market.

The ANZ jobs ads index, which measures the number of job advertisements in major papers, jumped 16.7 percent in April the biggest monthly gains since records began in 1975. Analysts said the data were regarded as secondary by the market but did have a good track record as a leading indicator of employment growth.
In this regard, they boded well for a pick-up in the very lacklustre pace of jobs growth this year and made it a little less likely official rates would have to be cut again.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the local currency had crept up to US$0.7830/35 from an early US$0.7819 low, to stand barely changed from Friday's late US$0.7831/36.

Traders said volumes had been light with the market thinned by a holiday in Japan, but there had clearly been good bids beneath US$0.7820 which reinforced this level as the one for bears to beat short term.

Resistance had proved equally stiff at US$0.7860 while defeating several upside attemnpts last week and analysts reckoned jobbing between these two levels would be a safe, if unexciting, trading policy for the moment.
On the crosses it was steady at 99.02/12 yen from 99.15/25 late here Friday with the absence of Tokyo keeping trade thin but dealers expecting continued demand from this quarter.

Japanese investors were big buyers of A$ government bonds and yen/A$ dual currency samurai issues last week as yield spreads widened to the local dollar's advantage, and there was talk of more samurais in the pipeline for this week.

The expansion, and in some cases restoration, of the A$'s yield premium over the U.S. dollar was partly due to a perceived lessening in the risk of a cut in official rates following uncomfortably robust wages data for the MArch quarter.

Dealers said there were still whispers the Reserve Bank board would decide to sanction a cut at its monthly meeting Tuesday, but might delay the move from the usual slot of Wednesday morning to instead coincide with testimony on the economy by governor Ian Macfarlane on Thursday.
Macfarlane gives his first testimony on the course of monetary policy, the Australian equivalent of Humphrey Hawkins, to a Parliamentary committee at 10.00 am on Thursday.
Shortly afterwards crucial employment data for April are released, and it has been the unexpected weakness of this indicator that has largely fuelled talk of another rate cut.
Analysts noted the RBA did not know what the data would reveal beforehand so might be wary of cutting in cease employment bounced more robustly than presently expected.
Median forecasts are for jobs to rise 35,000 in April after falls of 33,900 in March and 7,200 in February.
The very strong ANZ jobs ads might could lead some to nudge up their estimates for employment, although analysts emphasised the correlation between monthly figures was not that close.
What was certain, was that a cut has not been priced in and the dollar would test US$0.7720 in a hurry if one came.
